channel.title: Workbench
channel.description: Updates for Workbench, a Mac app for running Claude Code.

item.title: Workbench 0.9.5
item.description:
Here's what's new in today's update to Workbench.

Ask a side question with /btw

Start a message with /btw and the message box turns into a side question: a "btw" chip appears in front of what you type, and a hint reminds you that the answer stays out of the conversation.

Claude answers in a card above the box, with everything it knows about the conversation so far, while the conversation itself carries on untouched. Copy the answer, or close the card when you're done. Side questions can only be answered, so Claude can't run commands or change files from one.

To go back to a normal message, press Escape, or Delete at the start of the line. Side questions work from the iPhone and iPad app and from your other Macs too.

Pair your iPhone without Tailscale

You no longer need Tailscale to use Workbench on your iPhone or iPad. Workbench on your Mac shows a pairing code right away, and the app connects over your home Wi-Fi. If you do use Tailscale, Workbench still prefers it, and falls back to Wi-Fi when Tailscale is off.

To get the Wi-Fi connection on a phone you already paired, update the iPhone app and pair it again once.

Copying that pastes properly

The copy button on a message, and any text you select in the chat, now copy as formatted text and as Markdown. Paste into Mail or Notes and you get headings, lists and links. Paste into a plain-text field or a terminal and you get the Markdown.

Fixes and smaller changes

  • Tabs animate as they open and close.
  • Every Claude tab shows on the sidebar card. A project's card used to describe only one of them.
  • Tab moves to the next field in a form prompt box.
  • The ⌘ number hints in the sidebar wait until you hold Command, and no longer shift the rows around.
  • Paths with ~ stay intact in the chat. Text between two ~ characters used to get a line through it.
  • Messages that end on an @ file mention send. They used to sit unsent in the terminal.

item.title: Workbench 0.9.4
item.description:
Here's what's new in today's update to Workbench.

Commands that are easier to follow

The commands Claude runs read much better in the chat now.

  • Quiet rows for quick looks. When Claude only reads a file, searches or checks git status, it shows as a single quiet line, like "Read PantryStore.swift lines 10–20". Click it to open the file.
  • Claude's own words first. A command card leads with Claude's description of what it's doing, like "Ran the tests", with the command underneath. While it runs, a timer ticks so you know it's still going.
  • The output you care about. Short output shows in full. Longer output shows the last few lines, where the results usually are, with Show all for the rest.
  • Past tense when it's done. Finished commands read "Ran", "Read", "Searched for" and so on, so you can tell at a glance what already happened.
  • Files written from the shell look like files. When Claude writes a file with a shell here-document, the chat shows it like any other file Claude wrote, with its contents and line count.

Pictures, front and center

Click a picture in the chat and it opens over the whole Workbench window instead of in a small sheet. Pinch to zoom with your trackpad, or double-click. The viewer fades in gently and darkens toward the edges, so the picture stands out.

Right-click a picture, in the chat or in the full-screen viewer, to Copy Image or Save Image….

Rename a tab

Right-click a tab and choose Rename Tab… to give it a name of your own. Use Default Name puts the original back.

Fixes and smaller changes

  • Claude's question stays in view while subagents work. It used to get pushed out of sight as subagent updates came in.
  • The copy button sits at the bottom of Claude's replies. You no longer have to scroll back up to copy a long reply you just finished reading.
  • Active projects with no open tabs move down. In the Active list, projects you're working in now come first.
  • Smoother scrolling past plans in the chat.
  • Checking this Mac's HTTPS address is more reliable. The check skips system proxies, and if it fails, it says what went wrong.

Workbench for iPad

The iPhone and iPad app now has a Mac-style layout on a wide iPad: projects on the left, the chat in the middle, and Changes, Files and Artifacts on the right. That update is on its way to the App Store now.

item.title: Workbench 0.9.3
item.description:
Here's what's new in today's update to Workbench.

Move your setup to another Mac

Settings › General has a new Move to Another Mac section. Export saves your setup to one file, and Import on the other Mac brings it in. You choose which parts come along, both when you export and again when you import: projects and sidebar, shortcuts, appearance, other settings, Claude accounts, and paired Macs. Whatever an import replaces is backed up first.

Shell commands look like shell commands

Start a message with ! and the message box turns into a shell prompt. The ! becomes a chip, your command is set in the code font, and Send becomes Run. There's no need for a space after the !. Press Delete at the start of the line, or Escape, to go back to a normal message.

See how long Claude worked

After a run of 30 seconds or more, the chat shows how long Claude worked and when it finished, just like the terminal does.

Choose the command Claude tabs run

Settings › Claude has a new Command field. Leave it empty for plain claude, or type your own, like claude --permission-mode acceptEdits or the path to a wrapper script. Workbench warns you if a command would break a tab, and Use Default puts it back.

Fixes and smaller changes

  • Switching Macs no longer makes the pills jump. Clicking between This Mac and another Mac in the sidebar used to send the pills to the top of the sidebar and slide them back down.
  • The message box shows a border while you type in it. The border was there all along, hidden behind the glass.
  • A ! on its own can't be sent. It used to go to Claude as a message.

item.title: Workbench 0.9.2
item.description:
Here's what's new in today's update to Workbench.

A steadier chat

Numerous updates to make the chat view more stable and faster, and to make sure it never shows you a blank screen ever again.

Drag tabs to reorder them

Tabs can now be dragged along the tab bar, and the other tabs move out of the way as you go. A split pair moves together as one tab.

Fixes and smaller changes

  • Ctrl-Tab works in every tab. Ctrl-Tab and Ctrl-Shift-Tab used to switch tabs only from a terminal. In a chat, the message box treated them as typing. Now they step through the project's tabs from anywhere in the main window.
  • Clicking near a tab's close button selects the tab. The gaps around a tab's title and close button used to grab the window instead, so a click there could drag the window out of its tiled spot.
  • Quit Workbench Completely means completely. With Keep Working on, this now ends the Claude tabs Workbench was keeping running, too.

item.title: Workbench 0.9.1
item.description:
Here's what's new in today's update to Workbench.

Queue prompts while your Mac is asleep

Have an idea while you're out? Open a project in the iPhone app and queue a prompt. When your Mac wakes up, Workbench starts it as a new agent on its own branch, with nothing for you to confirm. Your project list stays on your phone while the Mac is offline, and prompts are encrypted so only your devices can read them. Needs the iPhone app 1.1.1, rolling out now.

Up arrow brings back your last message

In the chat, press up in an empty message box to get back what you sent last, just like the terminal. Keep pressing to go further back, edit, and send again.

Fable is marked amber

Fable uses your plan limits faster than the other models, so its name under the message box is now an amber capsule with a flame. In the model list, Fable says so and Haiku gets a leaf as the light, economy model.

Smaller changes

  • Anonymous usage counts now include which Claude model a session uses and when you switch. "Share anonymous usage data" in Settings turns this off, as before.

item.title: Workbench 0.9.1
item.description:
Here's what's new in today's update to Workbench.

Mention files with @

Type @ anywhere in a chat message to pick from the project's files and folders, the same way you would in Claude Code's terminal. Use the arrow keys and Tab or Return to choose one. Picking a folder fills in @Sources/ and keeps suggesting what's inside it, so you can drill down to the file you want. This works for remote Mac tabs too.

Slash commands in the middle of a message

You no longer have to start a message with a command to use one. Type something like "clean this up with /uns" and Workbench suggests /unslop. Commands that only make sense on their own, like /clear or /model, still only show up when they're the whole message.

Select across a whole reply

On the Mac, you can now drag across several paragraphs, headings, and list items in Claude's reply and copy them all at once. Before, each paragraph had to be selected on its own. Code blocks and tables are still selected separately.

Fixes and smaller changes

  • SSH works in Workbench tabs again. If your Ghostty config turned on its SSH shell features, running ssh in Workbench failed with "Unknown command: ghostty". Workbench now turns off just those two features and keeps the rest of your settings.
  • New Claude tabs work after logging out. With Keep Working on, logging out of your Mac and back in could leave new Claude tabs stuck at "Login incorrect". Workbench now notices and starts fresh, and your conversations pick up where they left off.
  • Your message stays when you change models. Picking a model from the model name under the message box used to erase what you'd typed. Now it stays put.
  • A new home on the web. The Workbench website is now at [workbenchapp.dev](https://workbenchapp.dev). Old links still work.

item.title: Workbench 0.9
item.description:
Here's what's new in today's update to Workbench.

Keep working

Sometimes you want to restart Workbench, but you don't want to interrupt your agents. So you wait for them to be done. And they keep going so you wait some more.

This is off by default for now, but there is a new feature you can enable from the general settings called "Keep Working". When this is enabled, your Claude Code sessions operate independently of the Workbench UI. What this means is that if you have 1, 2, or 20 agents grinding away on stuff, and the next Workbench update shows up, you can install it and restart without slowing your agents down at all.

I'm not the first person to implement something like this by any means, but it's so cool once you get used to having this.

Performance improvements

I've been adding a lot of features to the app, and this release is clearly no different, but I did take some time to go through some of the core code flows in the project and make sure that they were solid. And I took a look at some of the performance issues in the app and figured out ways to make them better.

There's more to do here for sure, but hopefully some things will feel a bit more zippy than before.

Switch models and effort from the chat

Type /model in the chat, or click the model name under the message box, to get the same list of models Claude Code shows in its terminal. The list sets effort too! On iPhone, tap the model name at the top of a session, or send /model as well.

Run a command from the chat

Start a message with ! to run it in the shell, the way you would in Claude Code's terminal. This works from iPhone as well.

See when Claude edits another project

Sometimes you have related projects, and while your chat exists in one of them, you need it to update a different one. Previously that was effectively impossible to track, but now the right sidebar shows you what other projects are being edited by Claude in a new "Also Changed" section.

Commit, push, and open a PR in one click

The Changes panel has Commit, Push, and Open PR buttons. Each one sends a message to the project's Claude tab, and Claude does the git work, so the buttons work with GitHub, GitLab, or anything else. Reword them, reorder them, or add your own in Settings › Shortcuts › Claude Actions.

Better narrow windows

Sometimes you just want a narrow window, and Workbench now does this better than before. As the window gets smaller, the side panels will collapse to make sure you can still see the chat and you can still see them as needed. Also when the project sidebar is collapsed, you can still see project icons, so you can navigate from a more streamlined view if you prefer.

A new app icon

Workbench has a new icon that's more fun! Five others are available, from Settings › Appearance on the Mac or in the iPhone app's settings.

Appearance settings

Colors, fonts, and text size have their own page in Settings, with a live preview that changes as you do.

Appearance also has a new Motion setting, for when the sparkles and glows are more than you want:

  • Full is how Workbench looks today, and it's the default.
  • Calm stops the big effects, like the sparkles on a working project and the glow on the start page. The small spinners keep moving, so you can still tell when Claude is working.
  • Still stops everything that moves on its own.

Calm and Still also use less of your Mac's power, so play with these if you want to make the app as light on your system as possible. If Reduce Motion is on in System Settings, Workbench uses Still automatically.

Fixes and smaller changes

  • Notifications from Claude. Claude can run bench notify in a Workbench tab to send you a notification on your Mac and your paired iPhone.
  • Lists in the message box. Type a dash or a number, then press Shift-Return (Return on iPhone), and the next line continues the list. Your own messages now show as Markdown, so lists read as lists.
  • File paths open in the Finder. Click a file path in Claude's reply to show that file in the Finder.
  • A steadier iPhone connection. A dropped connection is noticed within a minute, and a reply that didn't reach the Mac says so and gives you your draft back.
  • The version is in the sidebar. The bottom of the sidebar shows the version and build you're running.
  • Crash reports. If Workbench crashes, it sends a report so the bug can be fixed. It's part of Share anonymous usage data in Settings › General, so turning that off turns this off too.
  • Easier to install. Downloads now come as a disk image. Open it and drag Workbench into Applications.

item.title: Workbench 0.8.4
item.description:
Pick a color theme

Workbench now comes with 36 color themes. Choose one for light mode and one for dark mode in Settings › General › Colors, or while setting up, and Workbench switches between them with your Mac's appearance. The terminal tabs, sidebars, chat and diffs all take the theme's colors. If you'd rather keep your Ghostty theme, that's still an option.

Your theme's own color now shows up throughout, instead of the same orange everywhere: the Start Claude button, the send button, the checklist and timer, and the sidebar rows for sessions Claude is working on. Your messages in the chat view get a soft tint of it too, so they stand out from Claude's. A few themes have no color of their own, and those keep the orange.

Read Claude's plan in the chat

When Claude asks you to approve a plan, the chat view now shows the plan itself, so you don't have to switch to the terminal and scroll back to read it. Long plans fold after a screenful, with Show Full Plan to read the rest, and the question card has a Read the Plan button so you can read it all right before you answer. The iPhone app shows the plan too.

Clicking a file name in the chat now opens files outside the project, like Claude's plan files, in a read-only tab. Before, those looked like links but did nothing.

Close several tabs at once

Right-click a tab for Close Other Tabs, Close Tabs to the Right and Close All Tabs. If any of those tabs is still working, Workbench asks once instead of once per tab.

Fixes and smaller changes

  • Switching models feels instant. The model you pick shows right away, with a small spinner until Claude confirms. A switch made with /model in the terminal shows up right away too.
  • A quieter sidebar. The large card that popped up when you hovered over a project is gone.
  • Settings looks right in every theme. The strip at the top of Settings and the selected section now follow your theme, so they're easy to see on dark themes. You can also browse the themes with arrows, for mice that can't scroll sideways.
  • The New Agent sheet matches your theme. It no longer shows a dark box inside a light sheet when your theme and your Mac disagree on light or dark.
  • Pairing another Mac is easier to find. The switch in Settings › Remote Access is now called "Let my iPhone and other Macs connect", and the directions point to the + next to This Mac at the top of the sidebar.
  • No stray blue box on the welcome screens when Keyboard navigation is turned on in macOS.
  • "Left running" is the new name for processes still going after you close their tab, with a note on what that means.

For the iPhone app

With this version on your Mac, the iPhone beta can show code in color in diffs and files, open the whole file around a change with unchanged stretches folded away, review a commit by tapping it, and show file type icons. Phones that use Match Mac for their colors follow your Mac's theme, including its accent color.

item.title: Workbench 0.8.3
item.description:
Send Feedback is always there

The feedback button at the top right now stays put when the right panel is open. Before, it often disappeared to make room for the panel's Changes, Files and Artifacts switch. Now that switch makes room instead. Workbench is in beta, so please keep the feedback coming.

Fixes

  • Approve Claude's plan from the chat view or your phone. When Claude asked you to approve a plan, the chat view and the iPhone app used to tell you to answer in the terminal. Now they show the choices as buttons, like Claude's other questions.
  • The Files view shows every folder in a project folder that holds several repos. Before, it could run out of room on one repo's build output and leave later folders off the list.

item.title: Workbench 0.8.2
item.description:
A cleaner, glassier window

The tabs now sit up in the title bar, so the whole top of the window is one tidy strip and your work gets more room. The open tab flows straight into what's under it.

The message box is now glass, and the conversation scrolls underneath it. The same glass shows up on the other things that float: the jump-to-latest button, the checklist and agents bars, the slash-command list, the usage and Mac meters at the bottom of the sidebar, and the command bar (⌘K).

  • The Terminal | Chat switch now appears when you point at a Claude tab, and slides between the two.
  • Shortcuts and past sessions moved into the + menu next to New Claude.
  • A split shows as one tab with both halves in it. Click the mark between them to put the panes side by side or one above the other, swap sides, or separate them back into two tabs.
  • When the message box holds more than fits, its text fades at the edges so you can tell there's more.

Reviewing changes is much nicer

Diffs and files now show code in color, using your terminal theme. Diffs show the whole file with the long unchanged parts folded away, so you see what changed in context. Click Show 13 lines to open a fold.

  • Changes | File in a diff's header flips between the diff and the whole file. The file view marks changed lines in its margin.
  • The up and down arrows in the header (or Control-Option-↑ and ↓) step from change to change, and on into the next file.
  • You can select across lines in a diff, copy without the line numbers, and search with ⌘F.
  • Clicking a file opens it in a preview tab that the next file you click replaces, so tabs don't pile up. Double-click a file to keep its tab.
  • Click a commit to review it on one page: its message, the files it touched, and every diff in one scroll. Review All does the same for everything on your branch.
  • Changed files show an icon for their type, and buttons to open them or show them in Finder when you point at them.

Fixes

  • Workbench no longer crashes when the window is narrow with both the sidebar and the right panel open.
  • Status colors (added, removed, done, failed) are easier to read in both light and dark mode.
  • VoiceOver can now name every control in Settings.

item.title: Workbench 0.8.1
item.description:
Split panes

Keep Claude and a terminal on screen together instead of flipping between tabs. Press ⌘D to open a shell beside the tab you're in, or ⇧⌘D to open one below it.

  • ⌘] or a click switches sides. The side you're typing in gets a ring, and the other side dims a little.
  • Drag the line between them to resize, or double-click it to make both sides the same size.
  • Already have the tab you want beside Claude, like your dev server? Right-click a tab and choose Split With.
  • Right-click the joined tab to stack the panes, swap sides, or unsplit. Splits come back after you quit and reopen.

Group projects your way

The sidebar can now use groups you make, like a backend and its apps together. Turn it on in Settings › General › Group projects, or View › Group Projects › Custom Groups.

  • Drag projects into a group, or right-click one and choose Move to Group.
  • Fold a group away when you're not using it. Projects you haven't grouped wait in Ungrouped.
  • By Activity, the Pinned, Active, Recent, and Inactive sections you have now, is still there if you prefer it.

Code in the chat stands out, and copies with one click

Variable names, commands, and file names in Claude's replies now take your terminal theme's blue, the way Claude Code shows them in the terminal, on a soft background. They're easy to spot even if you use a monospaced font for everything.

Click one to copy it. No more carefully selecting STRIPE_SECRET_KEY with the mouse. Code blocks have a copy button in their corner too.

Make the chat yours

Pick the chat's font, its code font, and its text size in Settings › General › Chat Text, with a preview as you go. While a chat is on screen, ⌘+, ⌘−, and ⌘0 change the size.

You can also choose the color of the ring around a split's focused side, in Settings › General › Appearance. The choices come from your Ghostty theme, so they still fit when you change themes.

Smaller improvements

  • ⌘1 to ⌘9 follow the sidebar, top to bottom, including your agents' worktrees. With another Mac's list showing, they open that Mac's projects.
  • Option-Backspace and Control-Backspace delete the previous word in the terminal, like they do in other Mac terminals.

Fixes

  • The chat no longer opens blank until Claude prints something.
  • On the Mac, a code block with a long first line no longer hides every line after it.
  • Quotes in the chat read like they do in the terminal: one unbroken bar, full-brightness text, and no cut-off lines around them.
  • When pairing another Mac over Tailscale fails, Workbench now says why, like a link from a different tailnet or HTTPS Certificates turned off. Before, it only said "Connecting".

On iPhone

Custom groups and the new code styling come to the iPhone app in its next TestFlight beta.

item.title: Workbench 0.8
item.description:
Get Workbench for iPhone

The iPhone app is in public beta on TestFlight. Answer Claude's questions, allow a command, or send a follow-up from your phone, and get a notification when a session needs you.

A small card at the bottom of the sidebar links to the beta. It goes away once you open it, close it, or pair a phone. The link is also in Settings › Remote Access and on the iPhone step of setup.

Updates no longer interrupt you

After an update, Workbench used to open What's New on top of your work. Now a small card at the bottom of the sidebar says which version you're on. Click it to see what changed, or close it.

Connecting to your Mac is more reliable

  • Renamed your Mac? Workbench now sets up Tailscale for the new name, so your phone and other Macs can connect again instead of failing.
  • Remote Access only reports it's working when it is. If HTTPS isn't working yet, the Mac you're connecting to says what's wrong, which is usually HTTPS Certificates being off in Tailscale.
  • Clearer errors. When a secure connection to another Mac fails, Workbench says what usually causes it and where to fix it.

Screenshots in feedback

Send Feedback now takes up to four screenshots, so it's easier to show what you mean. The form also uses standard Mac colors instead of your terminal theme.

Recaps and Brain Dump use the right Claude account

If you use more than one Claude account, recaps and Brain Dump now run on the project's own account instead of your main one, and what they use now shows on the Usage page. Brain Dump also splits up your messages with a smaller, faster model.

item.title: Workbench 0.7.20
item.description:
See your month's spending without a plan

If your Claude account has no plan limits, like an API key, a company gateway, or an Enterprise plan billed by usage, the foot of the sidebar now shows what you've spent this month. Before, some of these accounts showed nothing there.

  • Working to a quota? Set a monthly budget on the Usage page and the ring fills toward it.
  • It's an estimate. The number is worked out at standard API prices from Claude Code's logs on this Mac, so a negotiated rate or use on other computers won't be included.

All your projects in Brain Dump

Brain Dump used to stop at 10 project icons. Now it shows every one, so you can look through them while you decide what to work on. Point at an icon to see the project's name right away.

The top of the window acts like a title bar

Double-click empty space in the tab row or the panel header to zoom the window, the same as any other Mac app, and drag from there to move it. It follows your Mac's title bar double-click setting.

Updates install themselves when your Mac is idle

Updates now install by default after 30 minutes with no input, as long as nothing would be interrupted. Workbench restarts to do this, so this also applies when you step away from your main Mac. If you'd rather choose when, turn off Install updates when this Mac is idle in Settings. If you already turned it off, it stays off.

Also in this version

Workbench now keeps a small log on your Mac of how long chats take to open, to help track down chats that stay blank for a while. It has no conversation text in it and isn't sent anywhere.

item.title: Workbench 0.7.19
item.description:
A different Claude account for each project

Keep a work account for work repos and a personal one for everything else. Each project now picks which Claude account its tabs sign in with.

  • Settings › Claude Accounts lists each account with its email, plan, and how many projects use it. Add Account walks you through naming it, signing in, and choosing its projects.
  • Switch from the project's menu in the sidebar, or the button next to New Claude Tab. Right-click New Claude Tab for a one-off tab on another account.
  • Already use several accounts? Workbench finds them on your Mac and adds them for you.
  • Usage follows along. The sidebar rings show the selected project's account, and the Usage page has a card for each one.

Recaps and other background work still use your main account, and your phone and the menu bar still show its plan usage.

Worktrees you made yourself show up in the sidebar

Worktrees you made in a terminal or with Claude Code now appear under their project, wherever they live. Nothing starts until you open one.

  • They're yours. Workbench never deletes them, even with automatic cleanup on.
  • Don't want one listed? Right-click it and choose Remove from Sidebar. Its folder and branch stay put, and Show Hidden Worktrees on the project brings it back.

Choose where new worktrees go

Settings › General › Agents has a new setting for where new agents' worktrees go, with a folder for each repo inside the one you pick. The default is still next to the repo, and worktrees you already have stay where they are.

Links in chat look like links

Links in Claude's replies are now blue, and the pointer turns into a hand over them, so you can tell what's clickable.

item.title: Workbench 0.7.18
item.description:
Inactive projects start fresh

When a project moves to Inactive, whether it's gone a day without use or you chose Move to Inactive, Workbench now closes its tabs. Coming back to it shows the New Tab page instead of a Claude tab from days ago, so you can start something new or pick up a past session from the list.

  • Tabs that are still working stay open: Claude in the middle of a task or waiting on you, or a program like a dev server running in a shell.
  • The project you're looking at keeps its tabs until you leave it.
  • Workbench also starts faster with lots of projects, since it no longer resumes old Claude sessions in projects you haven't touched.

Settings › Remote Access

The iPhone page in Settings is now called Remote Access, since it's also where you pair an iPad or another Mac.

item.title: Workbench 0.7.17
item.description:
See what you've spent, if you use an API key

If Claude Code on your Mac runs on an Anthropic API key, or through Amazon Bedrock or Google Vertex, you pay by the token, and Workbench now shows it that way:

  • A Month ring in the sidebar takes the place of the plan rings. It shows what you've spent this month at API prices.
  • Set a monthly budget in Settings › Usage, for example to match your key's spend limit. The ring fills toward it, with a tick for how far through the month you are, and the card warns you once you pass 80%.
  • The Usage page opens with this month's spending, and no longer says "Your Claude plan covers this" when you don't have one.
  • On your iPhone, the strip above your projects reads like "Spent $312 of $500", and Usage and Costs starts with this month. This needs the next TestFlight build.

Workbench works out which kind of account you have from Claude Code itself, including an API key set in your shell profile. The total comes from Claude Code's logs on this Mac, so anything else that uses the same key isn't counted. If you're on a Pro or Max plan, nothing changes.

Send Feedback

There's a new Send Feedback button in the toolbar and in the Help menu. Tell me what's broken, confusing, or missing, or what you love. Every message is read.

Also

  • Switches in Settings and the welcome are now drawn in Workbench's own colors, so they're easy to read in dark mode and match your terminal theme.

item.title: Workbench 0.7.16
item.description:
Pick which projects notify your iPhone

Your phone now only gets notifications for the projects you choose. Right-click a project in the sidebar and choose Send Notifications to iPhone. A bell on its row shows it's on. The setting is off for every project to start, so turn it on for the ones you care about after updating. Worktrees follow their project.

A Lock Screen dashboard

With the latest Workbench beta on your iPhone, tap the Lock Screen button at the top of Projects to keep every Claude session on your Lock Screen at once: what needs you, what's working, and what's done. This Mac keeps it up to date. Workbench no longer starts a Lock Screen activity for a session on its own.

Do more on another Mac from this one

When a project on another Mac is on screen:

  • Start an agent and pick the branch it starts from. It branches from main like the New Agent sheet would, copies the suggested .env files, and no longer hangs on Starting if the connection drops. New Agent on a Branch is in the right-click menu too.
  • Close Claude tabs, and clean up or discard agents, with the same warnings you'd see on that Mac.
  • Run and stop tab shortcuts like the dev server, and see which ports they're on.
  • ⌥⌘N opens Brain Dump for that Mac, and ⌘T, ⇧⌘T and ⇧⌘N act on that project instead of the last one on this Mac.
  • The Changes panel looks like it does for local projects: grouped by folder, with the branch header showing ahead/behind and push state. Refresh and the compare-against picker work too.
  • Work there uses the same orange working animation as work here. The blue Mac name is the only sign a project is remote.

Update Workbench on both Macs for all of this.

Brain Dump

Send Tasks is now called Brain Dump, and its button sits in the top bar next to the sidebar toggle. Agents with long prompts now start reliably.

Easier setup

The welcome notices when Claude Code is installed but not signed in and offers a sign-in window right there (also in Settings). It also warns you before you continue without a tool Workbench needs.

Anonymous usage data

Workbench now shares anonymous counts of what you use, like how many agents you start, to help improve it. Never your code, prompts, project names, or location. Turn it off any time with Share Anonymous Usage Data in Settings.

item.title: Workbench 0.7.15
item.description:
Projects on your other Macs show what's going on

When you work on a project that lives on another Mac, the sidebar now shows as much as it does for projects on this Mac:

  • Hover card: rest on a remote project to see what you asked, what Claude last said, its task list, its latest actions, and its sub-agents, plus the branch, pull request, and last deploy.
  • More in each row: in the Standard layout, busy rows list the last few things Claude did, waiting rows show its question with Allow and Deny, and finished rows show the recap.
  • Task list and agents in the chat: with the right panel hidden, the chat pins Claude's task list or its sub-agents above the message box.

Update Workbench on both Macs to get all of it. A Mac on an older version still works, it just shows less.

Clearer progress everywhere

  • Steps read in plain words. "Ran git log --oneline -30" now reads "Showed recent commits". Permission prompts still show the exact command, so you always see what you're allowing.
  • A busy project's hover card starts with the work under way: your prompt, Claude's latest note, its steps, and its recent actions.
  • Clicking anywhere on a sidebar row opens the project, even while its hover card is showing.

A cleaner Send Tasks screen

Each task is now a simple card with the project's icon, its branch, and the full prompt, which you can edit in place. Tasks Claude couldn't match to a project are marked so you can pick one.

One strip of meters

CPU, memory, and your plan limits now sit together as one row of small rings at the bottom of the sidebar. They stay grey until something needs your attention.

Removed

The morning summary ("Since Yesterday" and the Overview summary card) is gone. It wasn't pulling its weight.

item.title: Workbench 0.7.14
item.description:
A roomier project list

The sidebar has a new Standard layout with room to see what each agent is up to without opening it:

  • While Claude works: the step it's on, the tool it's running, and the last few things it did, with how long ago each one ran.
  • When it needs you: its question and the command it wants to run, with Allow and Deny buttons right in the row.
  • When it's done: a fuller recap and how many lines changed, so you can decide whether to look now.

The layout you've been using is now called Compact. It's still there for long project lists, and if you already have projects you'll stay on it until you switch. Switch any time in View › Project List (Option-Command-1 for Standard, Option-Command-2 for Compact).

Phone notifications with no setup

Your iPhone used to need an Apple developer key on your Mac before it could get notifications. Not anymore: turn on notifications in Workbench on your phone and they just work.

Notifications are also private now. Your Mac encrypts what each one says, and only your paired phone can read it. This needs the new TestFlight build of Workbench for iPhone. Older phone builds still get notifications, just without the encryption.

item.title: Workbench 0.7.12
item.description:
Send Tasks moved to the Overview

Send Tasks has a home that matches what it does. The button that splits one message into tasks for several projects used to sit in the project tab bar, next to controls that only act on the current project, which made it look like a per-project action. It now lives at the top of the Overview, the page that spans every project. The Overview's empty state offers it too, so when nothing is running you can fan work out from right there.

The File menu command and ⌥⌘N still open it from anywhere.

item.title: Workbench 0.7.11
item.description:
Sections you can tell apart

Your current work stands out. Pinned and Active now sit together on a slightly raised panel at the top of the sidebar, so what you're working on reads as one block. The Add Project button moved onto the first section's title.

Recent is compact. The last day's projects use smaller rows without a status line, under a "Last day" label, so more fit and they read as a step down from what's active. Using one moves it back up to Active.

Inactive is quieter. Folded-away projects are compact and dimmed until you pick one.

The iPhone app gets the same treatment in its next TestFlight build: compact, lighter rows for Recent and Inactive, and pinned projects keep their card when you reorder them.

item.title: Workbench 0.7.10
item.description:
A calmer activity meter

The CPU and memory meter is easier to follow. The bars at the foot of the sidebar now update every 10 seconds instead of every few, and every 30 seconds while Workbench is behind other windows.

The project list in its card holds still. Resting the pointer on the meter still shows which projects are using your Mac, but the list refreshes every 10 seconds and is sorted by memory, which stays steady, instead of CPU, which swings from moment to moment. CPU numbers appear about 2 seconds after the card opens.

item.title: Workbench 0.7.9
item.description:
Sections, ⌘K, Send Tasks, and a Mac meter

Your projects now sit in four sections. Pinned holds what you've pinned. Active holds projects where Claude is working or waiting on you, or that you used in the last 6 hours. Recent holds the last day's work, and everything older folds away under Inactive. Projects in Active keep their place while you work instead of jumping to the top with every message. The "Keep projects active for" setting is gone, since these windows replace it.

Restarting no longer makes every project look busy. Workbench used to count a relaunch, when every Claude tab picks up its session again, as you using each project. It now goes by the last real message in each conversation, and the first launch of this version tidies up times that earlier restarts got wrong.

⌘K jumps anywhere. Press ⌘K, even from inside a terminal, type a few letters of a project, worktree branch, or menu command, and press Return. Picking a project with no tabs starts Claude there.

Send one message, start several agents. Send Tasks to Projects (⌥⌘N, or the orange button next to +) takes one message describing work across your projects. Claude splits it into one task per project, and you check each card (project, branch, and the exact prompt) before starting them all with ⌘↩. Each agent gets its own worktree.

See how hard your Mac is working. Two small bars at the foot of the sidebar show CPU and memory. They stay grey while things are fine and warm up under load. Rest the pointer on them to see which projects are using the most. It's built to cost almost nothing, and it stops while Workbench is hidden. You can turn it off in Settings › General.

The iPhone app shows the same four sections once its next update arrives. Until then it keeps its current two groups.

item.title: Workbench 0.7.8
item.description:
A faster phone

This update is mostly for the iPhone app, which gets a new build alongside it. Install both to get the full effect.

Conversations open and update without stalling on the phone. Workbench now sends the phone small copies of the screenshots in a conversation instead of the full pictures, and the whole picture only when you open one. A long session that used to arrive as several megabytes arrives as a few hundred kilobytes. It also sends the last stretch of a conversation first, with earlier messages a tap away, instead of everything at once.

The Mac's chat view is a little lighter too. Replies are parsed once rather than every time the conversation redraws, and rows that haven't changed are left alone.

Phones on the previous build keep working exactly as before. The new behavior switches on once the phone app updates.

item.title: Workbench 0.7.7
item.description:
Workbench 0.7.7 makes restarting, like for an update, much safer when you have several Claude sessions going. This update is the first that can do this, so it starts working from your next restart after installing it.

  • Every conversation comes back on its own. After a restart, all your Claude tabs pick their conversations back up right away, not just the one on screen. They show up in Overview, on your phone, and in notifications without you clicking through each one.
  • Pick up interrupted work in one click. If Claude was in the middle of something when Workbench quit, that tab now says the restart stopped it, with a Continue button. Continue asks Claude to carry on where it left off and sends any messages you had queued. The sidebar marks those projects so you can find them.
  • Drafts are kept. Text you typed but hadn't sent is still there after a restart, and so is an agent's first task if Claude hadn't started on it yet.
  • Restart When Claude Is Done. When an update is ready and Claude is busy, Restart to Update now names the busy tabs and offers to wait. Workbench restarts by itself as soon as Claude finishes everywhere.
  • A clearer progress bar. A busy project's checklist now shows as a bar inside its sidebar row, with a segment for each step and a count like 3/7, instead of a thin line along the edge.
  • Open buttons on published pages. When Claude publishes an artifact, its card in the conversation has an Open button again, on your Mac and your phone, and the page shows up in the Artifacts list.

item.title: Workbench 0.7.6
item.description:
Workbench 0.7.6 brings the cleaner project list from 0.7.5 to your iPhone.

  • Your phone's project cards match the Mac sidebar. Each card shows one line under the project name: what Claude is doing, or else the one thing that matters most, like failing checks or a failed deploy (in red), a deploy in progress, an open pull request, or a branch that isn't your default. Projects with nothing going on show just their name.
  • Deploys on your phone. Your Mac now sends deploy status to the phone, so you can see a deploy in progress or a failed one right on the project list.

Get the matching iPhone app from the latest TestFlight build.

item.title: Workbench 0.7.5
item.description:
Workbench 0.7.5 cleans up the project sidebar so it's easier to read at a glance.

  • One status line per project. Instead of the branch, pull request, checks, and deploy all squeezed onto one line, each project now shows the one thing that matters most: what Claude is doing, a problem like failing checks or a failed deploy (in red), a deploy in progress, an open pull request, or a branch that isn't your default. Projects with nothing going on take up a single line.
  • Details on hover. Rest the pointer on a project to see everything else: its branch, pull request and checks, the last deploy, local servers, and its folder. Click the pull request, deploy, or a server to open it.
  • A quieter right edge. Just the activity dot now. The pin and server icons moved into the details card.

item.title: Workbench 0.7.4
item.description:
Workbench 0.7.4 brings more of your Mac to your iPhone. With the latest TestFlight build of Workbench for iPhone, your phone can now:

  • Show what Claude Code has cost you. The phone's new Settings screen has a Usage and Costs page with the last 30 days at API prices, broken down by model, the same as the Usage page on your Mac.
  • Show the morning summary. Your Mac's daily summary of what Claude got done appears at the top of the phone's project list.
  • Pick which notifications you get. Turn off any kind on the phone (Claude needs you, Claude finished, pull request checks, deploys, or the morning summary) and your Mac stops sending it to that phone.
  • See which Mac is which. The phone shows each paired Mac's status and the version of Workbench it's running.

item.title: Workbench 0.7.3
item.description:
Settings, rebuilt

Settings now opens right in the Workbench window instead of a separate one. Press Command-comma and the sidebar turns into Settings' sections, with Back at the top to return to your projects. Each section follows your terminal theme like the rest of the app, and every setting explains what it does right underneath.

The sections are General, Claude (chat or terminal tabs, recaps, and the morning summary, with a button to write one now), Usage, Shortcuts, iPhone, Setup, and Updates. Usage and Costs lives in Settings now; Shift-Command-U and the plan rings in the sidebar still take you straight there.

item.title: Workbench 0.7.2
item.description:
Recaps of what Claude did

When Claude finishes a turn where it did some work, Workbench now writes a sentence about what got done, like "Fixed the login crash and opened PR #12. The build passes." Recaps show in the Overview, under a project in the sidebar that finished while you were looking elsewhere, and on your iPhone in notifications and Live Activities. A small, fast Claude model writes them on your own Claude plan, using very little of it, and they never show up in your past sessions. Turn them off in Settings > General.

A morning summary

Each morning at 8, Workbench sums up what Claude got done across all your projects since the day before: one line per project, plus anything left open. It sits at the top of the Overview next to pull requests whose checks failed or that are ready to merge, and arrives as a notification on your Mac and iPhone. Pick the time or turn it off in Settings > General, or choose View > Write Morning Summary Now any time.

Usage and costs

A new Usage and Costs page (Shift-Command-U, or click the plan rings at the bottom of the sidebar) shows how many tokens your Claude Code sessions on this Mac have used and what they would cost at Claude API prices: a daily chart by model, what prompt caching saved you, and breakdowns by model and project, with your plan's limits up top. It follows your terminal theme's colors. Claude Code clears out its old logs after about a month, so Workbench keeps its own daily totals and your history grows from here.

item.title: Workbench 0.7.1
item.description:
See your deploys land

After a pull request merges, Workbench follows the deploy of that change and shows how it went: Deploying, Deployed, or Deploy failed, right beside the branch in the sidebar and in the Overview. Click it to open your host's page for that deploy. When it finishes, you get a notification on your Mac, and on your iPhone if it's paired.

It works with hosts that report deploys to GitHub, like Railway, Vercel, Netlify, and Render. There's nothing to set up or sign in to beyond the GitHub CLI you already use for pull requests.

Fixes

Setup no longer says Tailscale isn't running when Workbench was opened from the Finder or the Dock.

item.title: Workbench 0.7
item.description:
Bench is now Workbench

Same app, new name. You'll see Workbench in the menu bar, the Dock, and throughout the app. Your projects, settings, iPhone pairing, and notifications all carry over, and nothing about how it works has changed. The app file in your Applications folder keeps its old name after this update; you can rename it to Workbench if you like. The bench command in your tabs still works the same way.

Name your projects

Projects no longer have to go by their folder's name. Right-click one in the sidebar and choose Rename… to give it any name you like. Press Return to save or Escape to cancel, and choose Use Folder Name to go back. Agents working on a branch of the project pick up the new name, and so do your iPhone, iPad, and other Macs.

item.title: Bench 0.6.4
item.description:
Much lighter on your Mac

Bench now uses a small fraction of the CPU it did before. The sidebar's animations (a working project's sparkles, the clouds for work on another Mac, the glow when Claude is waiting, and Claude's spinning symbol) used to be redrawn by Bench many times a second, and with a few projects busy that added up to about a quarter of a CPU core all day. macOS now plays them on its own. They look exactly the same, and Bench drops to around 1 to 5 percent while it's showing status. Better for your battery, and quieter fans.

item.title: Bench 0.6.3
item.description:
Slash commands in the chat

Type / in the chat view and Bench suggests matching commands, including your own and your plugins'. Use the arrow keys to pick one, Tab to fill it in, and Return to run it. Commands that open a picker, like /model, go to the terminal, where the picker shows.

This also brings slash command suggestions to the iPhone and iPad app.

Drag images into the chat

Drop image files anywhere on the chat view to attach them to your next message, the same as pasting. Other kinds of files are turned away.

Tell your other Macs apart

When the sidebar shows projects on another Mac, drifting clouds and that Mac's name sit behind them, so you always know you're not working on this one.

Also

The Claude mark in an empty chat is sharp again.

item.title: Bench 0.6.2
item.description:
Chat really is the default when you pick it

If you set Settings > General > Show new Claude tabs as to Chat, every new Claude tab now opens as a chat. Before, it only applied to tabs from the + button and ⌘T: a new project's first tab, and the tab for a new agent on a branch, still opened as a terminal.

item.title: Bench 0.6.1
item.description:
Tables look right in the chat view

Tables in Claude's replies now use the full width of the chat, like they do in the terminal. Short columns stay compact, long text wraps neatly inside its column, and rows no longer overlap each other. A table only scrolls sideways when it has more columns than can fit.

item.title: Bench 0.6.0
item.description:
Every page Claude makes, one click away

When Claude publishes an artifact for you (a dashboard, a mockup, a write-up), Bench now keeps track of it.

  • An Artifacts tab in the right panel, next to Changes and Files, lists every page Claude has published for the project, across all its conversations. Newest first, with which version it's on and which conversation made it. Click one to open it in your browser, or hover for Copy Link.
  • A card in the chat whenever Claude publishes or updates a page, with an Open button. No more digging links out of replies.
  • On your iPhone, the ••• menu in a conversation has Artifacts too. Tap a page to open it in the Claude app or Safari.

Folders without git look right

A project that isn't a git repository used to show a lonely "Not a Git Repository" message floating in the right panel. Now it gets a small note at the top with the project's files right below.

item.title: Bench 0.5.9
item.description:
Switch models right from the chat view

Picking a model in the chat view now just works. Before, Claude asked "Switch model?" in its terminal, out of sight, and the chat view got stuck until you went to the terminal to answer.

  • On a long conversation, the chat view asks first and explains the cost: the next reply re-reads the whole conversation on the new model, so it's slower and uses more of your limits. Short conversations switch right away.
  • Works from your iPhone too.
  • Typing /model in the terminal still gets Claude's usual question.
  • Claude tabs that were already open pick this up after they restart.

item.title: Bench 0.5.8
item.description:
Your Claude plan's limits, right in the sidebar

Three small rings at the bottom of the sidebar show how much of your 5-hour, weekly, and per-model (like Fable) limits you've used. No status line setup needed.

  • Pace tick: a small tick on each ring marks how far into that window you are. If the ring has passed its tick, you're using that limit faster than it refills.
  • Hover to see exact percentages and how long until each limit resets. Click for the details.
  • Your own status line keeps working exactly as before.
  • Turn the rings or the ticks off in Settings > General.
  • Paired iPhones show the same rings above the project list.

Also

  • File changes in the chat view show as solid blocks again, instead of rows of rounded lines.

item.title: Bench 0.5.7
item.description:
Bench 0.5.7 adds a start page for your projects and a new welcome for first launch.

  • A start page for every project. A project with no tabs open now shows its icon, a big Start Claude button, Shell and Agent on a Branch, your dev server and shortcuts, and your last few conversations to pick back up in a click. Projects on your other Macs get the same page.
  • The + button opens a New Tab page. Instead of a small menu, + shows the start page in place of your current tab. Pick anything, or click another tab, to close it. ⌘T still opens Claude right away.
  • A new welcome. First launch now walks you through checking your Mac's tools, choosing whether new Claude tabs open as a terminal or a chat, matching your terminal theme, adding projects (suggested from folders you've already used Claude Code in), and pairing your iPhone. See it any time with Help > Welcome to Bench.
  • Other Macs' projects fill the window. The view for a project on another Mac no longer shrinks to a strip in the middle.

item.title: Bench 0.5.6
item.description:
Bench 0.5.6 makes the sidebar sort itself, and lets you send queued messages right away.

  • Active projects take care of themselves. Projects you've worked in lately show under Active, most recent first. Sending Claude a prompt, opening a tab or starting an agent counts, and so does work Claude Code remembers from outside Bench. After a few days without use (3 by default, set in Settings > General) a project moves to Inactive, and it comes back as soon as you use it again.
  • Pin to Top. Right-click a project and choose Pin to Top to keep it at the top of Active. Drag pinned projects to put them in your order. Move to Inactive and Make Active are still there too.
  • The iPhone app matches. With the latest TestFlight build, your phone shows the same Active list and a folding Inactive section, with Pin to Top and Move to Inactive when you long-press a project.
  • Send queued messages now. A message you queued while Claude was busy has a Send Now button, which stops the step Claude is on and hands it your message, like Ctrl+Return in the terminal. Control-Return in the chat view's message box does the same.
  • Compacting no longer stretches the window. Running Compact from the chat view kept the content from fitting the window until it finished. Fixed.

item.title: Bench 0.5.5
item.description:
Bench 0.5.5 adds a few touches to the chat view's message box.

  • Claude's suggested next message. After a turn, Claude Code often guesses what you'll say next and shows it faintly in its terminal. That guess now shows faintly in the chat view's empty message box too. Press Right Arrow or Tab to fill it in, then Return to send. On iPhone it's a chip you can tap.
  • Shift-Return adds a line. Shift-Return (or Option-Return) starts a new line in the message box instead of sending.
  • Context reads with a slash, like "64k / 1M".

item.title: Bench 0.5.4
item.description:
Bench 0.5.4 makes the chat view quicker, smoother, and better at showing what Claude is up to.

  • See Claude's subagents. When Claude sends out agents, each gets a card in the chat with what it's for and what it's doing right now. While they run, they also show in the right sidebar under the checklist, so they don't scroll away. When a background agent or command finishes, a quiet line in the chat says so.
  • Sending feels instant. Your message shows the moment you press Return, and new messages slide in while the conversation glides up to make room.
  • See and change the model. The model Claude is using shows next to the context meter, as soon as a session starts. Click it to switch to Fable, Opus, Sonnet or Haiku.
  • Edit or remove queued messages. A message you sent while Claude was busy now has Edit and Remove under it. The other queued messages stay queued.
  • Compact or clear without typing. The new / menu next to the paperclip runs Compact Conversation or Clear Conversation.
  • Copy a message. Hover over a message and click the copy button beside it.
  • Your draft stays put. Text and pictures in the message box are still there when you switch projects and come back.
  • Picture previews. Pictures you attach or paste show as thumbnails instead of file names.
  • Right-click changed files. Files in the Changes sidebar have a menu to open them, show them in Finder, or copy their full or relative path. The Files tab can copy either path too.
  • Simpler context meter. Context use is now just text, like "64k of 1M", which turns orange and then red as it fills.

item.title: Bench 0.5.3
item.description:
Bench 0.5.3 makes the chat view easier to follow while Claude works.

  • The chat stays at the bottom. New text and tool steps used to pile up out of sight while Claude worked on a long turn. Now the chat follows along as the conversation grows. Scroll up to read something earlier and it stays put, with a button to jump back to the latest. Sending a message always brings you back down.
  • See messages you've queued. A message you send while Claude is busy now shows up right away as a Queued bubble under what Claude is doing. It becomes a normal message once Claude reads it. Before, it didn't appear until then, which could be a whole turn later.
  • Paste images into the chat. Press Command-V in the message box to attach a screenshot, a copied image, or image files copied in Finder. Text still pastes as text.

item.title: Bench 0.5.2
item.description:
Bench 0.5.2 opens long conversations much faster.

  • Big chats open in a moment. Long Claude sessions write transcripts of hundreds of megabytes. The chat view used to read all of it before showing anything, which could take several seconds. Now it reads from the end, just far enough to show the recent conversation, so even the biggest sessions open in well under a second. The top of the chat says when older messages are left out, and nothing in the transcript is changed.
  • Faster on your phone and other Macs too. They get the same speedup when they open a long session on this Mac.

item.title: Bench 0.5.1
item.description:
Bench 0.5.1 brings the chat view's step cards to your phone, and lets the phone dress in your terminal's colors.

  • Your phone in your Mac's colors. The Bench iPhone app (1.1 build 7 and later) can take on the background and text colors of your Ghostty theme, light or dark. You can turn this off from the phone's menu.
  • Edits, commands and Stop on the phone. The phone now shows the lines Claude changed, whether each command worked and what it printed, and a Stop button while Claude is working. This needs the new phone build too.
  • Other Macs get the same. When you watch a Claude session on another Mac, you see command results and can stop Claude from there.
  • Stopped commands say so. A command you stopped or denied now reads "Stopped" instead of "Failed".

item.title: Bench 0.5
item.description:
Bench 0.5 lets you read and run any Claude tab as a chat, right on your Mac.

  • Chat or terminal, per tab. Switch a Claude tab between its terminal and a chat with the buttons in the tab bar, or View > Show as Chat (⌥⌘T). Claude keeps running in the terminal either way, so the raw terminal is always one click away. Settings > General picks which one new Claude tabs start in.
  • In your terminal's colors. The chat uses your Ghostty theme, light or dark, so it looks like part of Bench rather than a separate app.
  • See what Claude did. Files it read sit on a quiet timeline, and you can click one to open it. Edits show the lines that changed. Commands show whether they worked and the last lines they printed.
  • Where you're reading. The end of the conversation shows what Claude is doing or that it's waiting on you, with a timer and a Stop button.
  • Answer with the keyboard. When Claude asks to run something, Return allows it and Escape denies it, just like in the terminal. Questions and permissions get cards right above the message box.

item.title: Bench 0.4.2
item.description:
Bench 0.4.2 makes answering Claude from your phone or another Mac smoother.

  • Trust a new folder from anywhere. When Claude starts in a folder it hasn't opened before, it asks whether you trust it before doing anything else. That question used to show up only in the Mac's terminal, so a session started from your phone got stuck. Now it appears as a card you can answer from your phone or another Mac. Bench only passes your answer along. It never trusts a folder for you.
  • Answers take effect right away. After you allow or deny a permission from another device, the card goes away as soon as Bench has your answer. Before, it stayed until Claude moved on, which made it look like the tap hadn't worked. Answered questions clear the same way, and the tab stops showing orange on the Mac.

Trusting a folder from your phone needs the latest Bench beta for iPhone.

item.title: Bench 0.4.1
item.description:
Bench 0.4.1 fixes two problems some people saw after updating to 0.4.

  • Your Active projects stay Active. Restarting Bench soon after opening it could move every project to Inactive. Bench now keeps your Active list no matter when you quit or update.
  • ⌘1 to ⌘9 always work. If your Active list was empty when Bench opened, the shortcuts for jumping between Active projects didn't come back after you marked projects Active again. They now follow the list as it changes.

If your projects moved to Inactive after the 0.4 update, mark them Active once more and they'll stay that way.

item.title: Bench 0.4
item.description:
Bench 0.4 tells you what's new, answers Claude's questions from anywhere, and gives the terminal a softer edge.

See what's new. When an update is ready, the button at the bottom of the sidebar shows what's in it before you restart. After Bench updates, a What's New window lists everything that changed since the version you last used. You can open it any time from Bench > What's New in Bench.

Answer Claude's questions from another Mac. When Claude asks you a multiple-choice question, you can now answer it while watching the session from another Mac: pick an option, tick several where it allows, or write your own answer. Bench enters it on the Mac where Claude is running. The tab also turns orange as soon as Claude asks, instead of a few seconds later.

Compacting is easy to spot. While Claude compacts a conversation you're watching from another Mac, a banner says so, and the conversation shows a clear "Conversation compacted" card afterward instead of a line of small gray text.

Answering questions and the compacting banner come to the iPhone app in its next update.

A rounded terminal. The terminal, diffs, and files now sit in the window as a card with rounded corners, below a tab bar that matches the sidebars.

Claude tabs that are already open pick up question and compacting detection the next time Claude starts in them.

item.title: Bench 0.3.1
item.description:
Bench 0.3.1 makes the window match your terminal.

Matches your terminal theme. The sidebar, toolbar, changes panel, diffs, and files now use the colors of your Ghostty theme, and the window goes light or dark to match it. If your theme switches between light and dark with the system, Bench follows along. Prefer the system look? Turn off "Match the terminal theme" in Settings > General.

Also:

  • The button that shows and hides the changes panel is back on the right side of the toolbar, above the panel it opens.
  • The app icon's chevron no longer shows a thin line through it.

item.title: Bench 0.3
item.description:
Bench 0.3 gets Bench ready for other people to use, and adds a few things you'll notice right away.

Your own tab shortcuts. Add one-click tabs for commands you run often in Settings > Shortcuts. They show up at the right of the tab bar and in the + menu, and can be limited to one project or to projects with a certain file. JavaScript projects also get a dev server button that runs dev with the project's package manager.

Setup checklist. Bench now checks for Claude Code, git, the GitHub CLI, and Tailscale, and shows what it found with links to anything missing. It appears once on first launch and lives in Settings > Setup. Bench also finds these tools the same way your shell does, so tools installed outside Homebrew work too.

Safer agent cleanup. When an agent's pull request merges, Bench only removes its worktree if nothing would be lost: no uncommitted or unpushed work. Removed worktrees go to the Trash. Automatic cleanup is now a setting in Settings > General, and it's off by default.

Updates ask first. New installs ask before checking for updates. Installing an update while the Mac is idle is now a setting in Settings > Updates, off by default.

iPhone companion.

  • Bench no longer replaces an existing Tailscale Serve setup. If something else is using it, Bench uses a /bench path instead.
  • The phone can only read files that show up in the project's file list.

Also:

  • Bench > Acknowledgements credits Ghostty, Sparkle, and the other open source projects Bench is built on.
  • Bench saves less of what Claude passes to its tools. Whole file contents no longer sit in Bench's support folder.

item.title: Bench 0.2
item.description:
This is the first version of Bench that keeps itself up to date.

  • Automatic updates. New versions download in the background. They install when you quit Bench or click Restart to Update at the bottom of the sidebar. If Claude is busy, Bench asks before restarting, and Claude tabs pick up their conversations afterward. A Mac nobody is using installs updates by itself after 30 minutes with nothing running.
  • Files sidebar. The right sidebar has a Changes / Files switch. Files shows the project's folders and updates as files come and go. Click a file to open it in a tab with line numbers that reloads as Claude edits it. This works for projects on your other Macs too.
  • Your messages in remote conversations. Messages you send while Claude is busy, and messages that start with a paste, now show up when you watch a session from another Mac or your iPhone.

Settings has a new Updates tab with the version and a switch for automatic checks.
